This package is built to help build custom solutions using version 2 of EliteForm's API. It requires an EliteForm account and an API key, so please consult with your EliteForm representative first. Keys for the original `/api/v1` endpoints do not work with this version of the package. If you are moving a script from version 1, see `NEWS.md` for what to change.

## Installing the Package

Install eliteformR from GitHub with the remotes package:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("EliteFormLLC/eliteformR")

# To also install these guides, so vignette(package = "eliteformR") lists them.
# This is slower and needs pandoc, which RStudio includes.
remotes::install_github("EliteFormLLC/eliteformR", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

## Creating Token

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Load the eliteformR package
library(eliteformR)
```

To create your API Token, call `EF_CreateAPIToken()` with your key. The key identifies your organization, so no URL is needed. Treat the key like a password and keep it out of your scripts, for example in an environment variable.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Initialize Token
token <- EF_CreateAPIToken(Sys.getenv("ELITEFORM_API_KEY"))
```

Once the API Token has been initialized, pull your Team IDs and update your token with the one you want.

```{r eval = FALSE}
# Get all Team IDs
teams_df <- EF_GetTeamsList(token)

teams_df

#   id     name
# 1  1 Football
# 2  2 Softball

# Update the Token's Team ID
token <- EF_UpdateTokenTeam(token, 1)
# or
token <- EF_UpdateTokenTeam(token, teams_df$id[1])
```

Now you can begin running the other functions. An example is provided below that gets all sets from a particular day:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Get the completed sets for today, including Paperless
all_sets_df <- EF_GetAllSets(token)

# Get the completed sets for a specified date
all_sets_df <- EF_GetAllSets(token, "08/03/2026")

all_sets_df[, c("athleteId", "exerciseId", "setNumber", "repsCompleted", "actualWeight", "avgVelocity")]

#   athleteId exerciseId setNumber repsCompleted actualWeight avgVelocity
# 1        13         95         1            23            0          NA
# 2         6         88         1             5          225        0.61
# 3         6         88         2             4          235        0.55
```

## Getting Names

Sets, reps and maxes identify athletes and exercises by ID. To add names, join them to the roster and the exercise list. These two calls need the `ReadAthletes` and `ReadTeams` scopes on your key.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
roster_df <- EF_GetAthleteInfo(token, includeArchived = TRUE)
exercises_df <- EF_GetExercises(token)

named_sets_df <- merge(all_sets_df, roster_df[, c("athleteId", "firstName", "lastName")], by = "athleteId", all.x = TRUE)
named_sets_df <- merge(named_sets_df, exercises_df[, c("id", "name")], by.x = "exerciseId", by.y = "id", all.x = TRUE)
```

The roster leaves out archived athletes unless you pass `includeArchived = TRUE`, but their sets are still returned. `all.x = TRUE` keeps every set, with NA for any name that can't be found. Without it, `merge()` silently drops those rows.

## When There Is No Data

A call that matches nothing returns a data frame with no rows and no columns, so check `nrow()` before using a column in a script that runs unattended.

## Rate Limits

Each key may make 60 requests per minute, 600 per hour and 1,200 per day by default. Every function pulls all pages of its results, at up to 1,000 rows per request, and each page counts as one request. If the per-minute limit is reached, the package waits and retries. A longer wait stops with an error. To read many days, pass a range as shown in [Getting all Reps and Sets](get-reps-and-sets.Rmd) rather than calling once per day.
